adjudication_label: batch_1:Hall-Petch hardening and yield strength predictions
canonical_question: How do the grain sizes of the CrMoNbWV alloy produced by MA/SPS compare to those from arc melting to validate the Hall-Petch hardening contribution?

question_variants.question: How do the grain sizes of the CrMoNbWV alloy produced by MA/SPS compare to those from arc melting to validate the Hall-Petch hardening contribution?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text mentions grain size (1.24 µm) for a cited NbMoTaWVCr alloy and density comparisons, but it does not provide specific grain size values for the CrMoNbWV alloy produced by MA/SPS versus arc melting to allow for a direct validation of the Hall-Petch contribution.

answers.answer: A cited work reports a grain size of 1.24 µm for an NbMoTaWVCr alloy obtained by MA and SPS. The text notes the density of CrMoNbWV is lower than these alloys but does not report the specific grain size for the CrMoNbWV alloy produced by MA/SPS or arc melting to validate the Hall-Petch relationship for that specific comparison.
answers.mechanism: Fine grains contribute to high mechanical properties.
answers.boundary_limitation: No grain size data provided for CrMoNbWV alloy from arc melting or the specific MA/SPS route for validation of the Hall-Petch constant.
evidence_spans: Nevertheless, in Reference [ [2] ], an NbMoTaWVCr alloy with an extremely high yield strength of 3416 MPa and good plasticity of 5.3% at room temperature was obtained.
Volume fractions of Laves phase (Cr,V) 2 (Ta,Nb) and oxide phase Ta 2 VO 6 in this alloy were 7.7% and 6.2%, respectively.
According to the authors, the high mechanical properties were achieved by forming an interstitial solid solution in the matrix and by fine grains (1.24 µm).

source_evidence_spans: Simultaneously, the density of the CrMoNbWV alloy is lower than that of NbMoWVTa and NbMoWVTaCr HEAs.
